competition_formats.summary: Rocky Lake hosts at least TWO distinct competition formats. The scoring math determines the rig category — they are NOT interchangeable.

formats.name: One by One (sport / 1pt-per-fish)
formats.scoring: Primary score = count of fish caught. Secondary score = total weight. Bait restricted to insect/worm.
validated_rigs: TeleDragon 23' + Hydra 3000 + Mono .005" (2 Lb) + X-Series Slim Float + Hook #2 + Maggots at 22" depth (AM comp MVP — 19 fish in 30 min)
TeleValentine 23' + Heartspinner 2500 + Mono ~2 Lb + Hook #4 + Mayflies at 12" depth (PM practice — opened the second panfish layer)
formats.sequence_tactic: Validated 2026-06-05 3rd return. Cast TeleValentine (12" mayflies) FIRST at each spot as the 'scout' — shallow layer commits faster. If it hits, immediately follow up the EXACT SAME SPOT with TeleDragon (22" maggots) — ~50% hit rate on the follow-up within ~15 sec. Active panfish zones are STRATIFIED across both depth layers; the shallow hit signals the deep layer is also live at that spot. If TeleValentine hasn't hit by ~30 sec, the spot is cold — move on without burning a follow-up cast. Estimated catch-rate lift on confirmed-hot zones: ~50%.
formats.best_finish: Top-25 estimated (19-fish primary score, 30% behind top-4 leaders who hit 40-50 fish — exact placement pending leaderboard data)
open_variables: Wait-time cutoff (currently recasting at ~45 sec; top players likely cut at 20 sec)
Specific zone clustering — map leader positions next session
Hook size sweep (#4 vs #2 confirmed; try #6 for faster commits)
Bait sweep (worm vs maggot vs mayfly — partial data only)
skip_list: Colorado Golden Trout unique — 1.5-2.5 min hit time burns count points; skip in this format
Match rods (OmniFloat 14'10" SE measured 2x slower per cycle with identical tackle in PM A/B test)
Spinning/casting rods — reel-in cycle disqualifies the entire category

competition_formats.rig_category_rule: MATCH the rig to the scoring math, NOT the species. 1pt/fish = telescopic. Weight-quality = casting/spinning + selectivity. Mixing categories loses by definition (match rod with sport tackle = 2x cycle penalty).

slots.rod: OmniFloat 14'10" SE (Match Rod, 3-7.5 Lb, Moderate) — REJECTED for sport comp
slots.rejection_reason: Field-tested 2026-06-05 PM against TeleValentine 23' with IDENTICAL tackle (same line/hook/bait/float/depth) — measured ~2x slower per fish cycle. The bottleneck is the rod-type cadence (cast → drift → reel-in slack → recast), NOT the rig. OmniFloat got marginally longer casts but the doubled cycle time made the extra reach uneconomic. SINCE OmniFloat is the LIGHT match rod in inventory, any heavier match rod is worse — entire match category disqualified for Rocky Lake 1pt/fish sport competitions.
slots.salvage_role: Reserve for trout-weight or selectivity formats where individual fish quality matters more than count cadence. Even then, the SharpCaster (slot 3) is the stronger trout-comp rig.

critical_warnings: FORMAT MISMATCH = LEADERBOARD GAP. The biggest mistake at Rocky is running the wrong rod CATEGORY for the comp format. Match rod in a 1pt/fish comp = 2x cycle penalty (PM 2026-06-05 A/B confirmed). Telescopic in a weight-quality trout comp loses selectivity.
MATCH RODS ARE OUT for Rocky sport formats. OmniFloat 14'10" SE (the light match) was 2x slower than TeleValentine 23' with identical tackle. Heavier match rods are worse.
COLORADO GOLDEN TROUT UNIQUE = 1.5-2.5 min hit time. Worth pursuing in weight/size formats (potential 2nd-place secondary score) but BURNS count points in 1pt/fish formats. Skip in sport comps.
OVER-RATED LANDING WORKS on telescopic — 2 Lb mono landed 3.1 lb Trophy White Sucker because the rod blank absorbs the load (no drag mechanism to fail). Don't be afraid of ultralight line.
30% LEADERBOARD GAP in the 6/5 sport comp (19 fish vs top-4's 40-50). The rig is correct; the remaining variables are WAIT TIME and ZONE SELECTION, not gear.
